The trace (T2) and the graders (T3) show nothing through the command until T4 runs a session. T1's second gate ('reading every case of plugin/evals/ without an error') has no command output that shows it: the command has no list or dry-run mode, and running it on plugin/evals runs the real scaffolds (which need vloop, python3 and git, and one of which exits non-zero off macOS). Round 2 (20261102-230926) found this too, and it is not fixed.
findings.evidence: Shape items 1-3; docs/domain/domain-model.md:210-213 (P-8); plugin/evals/README.md (gate-review-real-misses is macOS-only, and its scaffold needs vloop on PATH); A1 has no flag that lists cases without running them.

findings.section: Behaviour contract / A4 llm; Worked example o6
findings.summary: The llm judge is not specified well enough. (1) It does not say which field holds the judge's answer and cost. The json form puts them in `result` and `total_cost_usd`, which judge_cost_usd sums. (2) It does not say where the judge runs, or with which tools, settings and plugins. docs/guide/evals.md says the judge 'has no access to the workspace'. A `claude -p` started in the workspace can read files and loads the user's settings. (3) It does not say how the prompt is passed. A `focus: trace` of a long session passed in argv can exceed ARG_MAX. (4) In o6 one fake `claude` on PATH is both the agent under test and the judge, and nothing says how it tells the two calls apart. Round 2 raised (1) and (4).
findings.evidence: Brief A4 'The judge is claude -p with --model ... --output-format json, given the grader's body and the focus'; docs/guide/evals.md lines 'It has no access to the workspace'; worked example o6.
findings.fix: Pin the following: the judge runs in an empty temporary directory, outside the workspace. It gets its prompt on stdin. Its answer is the last non-empty line of the JSON's `result`, and its cost is `total_cost_usd`. Take any flag that turns off tools or settings from `claude --help` (this review could not run it). For o6: the fake tells the calls apart by `--output-format stream-json` (the agent) versus `json` (the judge).

findings.section: Behaviour contract / A1, A2, A4, A5 (literal values)
findings.summary: Several values that a gate or test will compare are still described rather than written. (a) The `phase` of a skipped case, in report.json and in the PHASE column (fixture-operate has no phase). (b) The NOTES column when --runs > 1: graders below 1 in any run, or in the mean? (c) The form of <d> in 'timed out after <d>': the flag as given ('20m') or Go's Duration.String ('20m0s')? (d) The llm grader's default focus, 'the final assistant text': the trace's last `text` event, or Claude's `result`? (e) That `input_match` is a Go regular expression. The real cases write it as one (`vloop\s+brief\s+check`, `state\.json|\.gitignore`). The worked example's `vloop schema validate` also passes as a substring, so a substring implementation passes every gate and scores the real cases wrong. (f) Which refusal wins when several A1 conditions hold, for example two required flags missing. Round 2 raised (a), (b), (c) and (e).
findings.evidence: A2 skip ('the reason no phase', no phase value); A5 report shape and NOTES column; A2 'timed out after <d>'; A4 tool_used 'whose input matches it'; plugin/evals/*/graders: 9 tool_used graders with regex input_match.
findings.fix: Write each value literally. For example: phase `-` for a skipped case. NOTES names the graders below 1 in any run, in name order. <d> is printed as Duration.String(). The default focus is the last text event. input_match is a Go regexp searched in the input. Refusals are checked in the table's order, and missing flags in the order --agent, --model, --out.

findings.summary: 'Started as vloop starts that phase' is not exactly true, and the brief does not name the difference. vloop run gives work, review and verify sessions VLOOP_PLAN_SHA256 (the hash `vloop task gate` checks) and an effort from config. The tool has no driver-held plan and no effort flag. Round 2 found this, and it is not fixed.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/iterate.go:650, 780, 956 (PlanSHA: guard.hash()); internal/cli/task_gate.go:30 (checks it only when set); internal/driver/session.go Spec.Effort.
findings.fix: Add one line to A2: the tool's sessions get no plan hash and no effort (or the effort config gives the phase in the workspace), and those are the only differences.

findings.summary: The grader frontmatter is nested YAML: `target:` and `focus:` hold maps of `source` and `path` in 60 of the 98 graders, and patterns are single-quoted with backslashes. go.mod has no YAML library, and nothing in the repository parses nested frontmatter. The brief does not say whether a task may add a module dependency (which a session would have to fetch) or must parse this narrow subset by hand. A planner will choose silently.
findings.evidence: go.mod (no yaml module); internal/cli/skills_test.go:175 frontmatter() returns map[string]string; grader shapes counted over plugin/evals/*/graders/*.md.
findings.fix: Decide and write it under 'Decided here'. Either: no new dependency, and the tool reads the subset the cases use (scalars, single-quoted strings, one level of nested map). Or: gopkg.in/yaml.v3, fetched by the operator before the run.

findings.summary: The last line needs a `vloop run` session, which the verify session cannot start. The brief does not name the test that covers it. A test already does: TestSessionArgs pins the argv ending in "--output-format", "json". Round 2 found this, and it is not fixed.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/session_test.go:17-21 (TestSessionArgs); guidelines.md 'Say which worked-example lines the verify session cannot run'.
findings.fix: Write beside the line: '(covered by TestSessionArgs, internal/driver/session_test.go, unchanged)'.

findings.summary: The acceptance leaves out environment it depends on. A Copilot session's COPILOT_HOME holds no login, so Copilot logs in through `gh auth token`, and gh must be logged in. gate-review-real-misses is macOS-only: its scaffold exits non-zero where grep accepts -P, which here is a run error and exit 1. The sessions run `vloop` from PATH, while the hook runs `--vloop`'s binary.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/README.md ('Copilot logs in with gh auth token: the GitHub CLI must be logged in'); plugin/evals/README.md (gate-review-real-misses is for macOS hosts; its scaffold needs vloop on PATH).
findings.fix: In the acceptance, state: on macOS, `gh auth status` logged in, and `go install ./cmd/vloop` so that the PATH vloop and the hook's vloop are the branch's.

findings.summary: Unsure. The event shapes are 'as observed on 2026-11-02', but no sample of either transcript is in the repository. The fixtures the tests use will be written from the brief, so a wrong field name only shows at acceptance. This repository's guideline takes external formats from the tool or its docs.
findings.evidence: grep for '"assistant.message"' and '"tool_result"' outside .vloop/state finds only this brief; .vloop/repo-guidelines.md (formats from the tool, never from memory).
findings.fix: Commit the observed samples, trimmed and masked, as the tests' transcript fixtures, or put them in docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md, and cite them. The acceptance run then settles the question.

decisions: A repository tool, not a `vloop eval` subcommand: sound, since the cases are not shipped.
Sessions run under the phase's fence, and a case's allowed_tools and max_turns are ignored: right for qualification, but scores are not comparable with claude plugin eval (the brief says so).
`--vloop` names the hook's binary rather than the tool building its own fence hook: sound. Consider defaulting it to the PATH vloop the sessions also use (it already does).
Claude's stream-json is used only by this tool: sound, and it keeps every vloop session unchanged.
The judge is always Claude, default `sonnet`, three votes by majority: sound. Three votes triple judge cost on the 50 llm graders.
One arm, no without-plugin baseline: sound.
Cases of skills vloop does not start (operate, create-brief) are skipped, not failed: verified, these are exactly the two cases.
Exit 1 only when a run errors, never on a low score: this differs from claude plugin eval's --threshold exit. Fine for a bench, worth saying in the README.

Qualifying rule: a model's mean is no lower than the phase's default Claude model's on every case, at 3 runs. With llm graders' noise, a strict 'no lower' at 3 runs may fail a model on chance. Consider a stated tolerance, or more runs.
transcript.jsonl is kept unmasked under --out, whereas session records are masked. Acceptable for a scratch directory, but not stated.
`path.Match` and a repeatable `--case`: sound (and it fixes the claude plugin eval quirk the README notes).
Unsupported grader types score 0: sound. No current case uses tool_order or baseline.
Default --timeout of 20m: no source cited. Fine as a default.
